BiblicalUsage: Shachar is the dawn itself, the breaking of the day. Hosea says the LORD's going forth is prepared as the morning, and Isaiah promises that light shall break forth as the morning for those who fast aright. The word even stands in the title of the psalm about the hind of the dawn, and the angels hastened Lot as the morning arose over Sodom.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every dawn is a small resurrection, the light returning after the dark. The God whose going forth is as the morning will not leave His people in the night forever.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
